I wonder if Scholar's philosopher's stone is alien in origin.  Then it would make sense for him to have an alien nemesis.  And, I figure he'll get a nemesis sooner or later.

I think it's reasonable to assume that a couple of the six heroes without a unique nemesis will get one in Wrath. Of those six, the ones most likely to have alien nemesis seem to be Scholar (if the stone is alien), KNYFE (if FILTER has alien enemies), or maybe Naturalist (as a defender of the Earth).

Naturalist would make an interesting nemesis for Deadline, since Deadline might view Naturalist as a sort of kindred spirit, while Naturalist would just see a weird alien terrorist.

posts.name: Unsafe_Bet
posts.cooked:
trudge:

(On the Marvel side of things, compare Annhilus, Warbird, the Kree Intelligence, and Super Skrull, who all have different styles and types of threats.  DC wise, Darkseid is pretty different from the various Lantern Core villains, or the Invaders from the Legion comics)

Of these, the only ones I consider at all distinctive are the Skrulls (because they shapeshift) and the Yellow, Red, and Black Lantern Corps (because they nail the "fear"/"rage"/"death" angles hard, plus they're all different species and many are really creative), and arguably Darkseid (he doesn't really count since he's a god, but he is a space-god so we'll say he half-counts).  Everything else is pretty much random generic sci-fi nonsense, not significantly different from the content of 100 different public domain alien-invaders movies from the 50s thru 70s.  I admit I don't know the Kree Intelligence, but the Kree in general are just blue humanoids; not much stands out there.  I couldn't possibly guess from a glance at some random space-ork grunt whether it was a servant of Annihilus, Thanos, the Dominators, or the dudes who ruled the Vega system before it was re-canoned as belonging to the Orange Lantern, rather than whatever the previous explaination for why the Greens weren't allowed in there.

Her name could fit a space pirate or trophy hunter just as easily as an invader, but that would step on Capitans and Ambuscade's assorted toes, respectively.

My hope is that "Warfang" is just a hereditary name handed down from the barbarian ages of her species, and that she's actually from a Crystal Spires and Togas planet which hopes to purify humanity's violent impulses with harp music and sexual promiscuity.  (Disclaimer: I do not actually hope this, but if it turns out to be true I'll laugh once.)
